title: Adi-lila, chapter 2. The Auspicious Invocation Indicating the Object: Determining the Truth of Caitanya
html:
“Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta”
Ādi-līlā
Chapter 2
The Auspicious Invocation Indicating the Object: Determining the Truth of Caitanya
(English translation from the Bengali, following the Gauḍīya Maṭha edition and the Anubhāṣya, 2026)

শ্রীচৈতন্যপ্রভুং বন্দে বালোঽপি যদনুগ্রহাৎ ৷
তরেন্নানামতগ্রাহব্যাপ্তং সিদ্ধান্তসাগরম্ ॥ ১ ॥

śrī-caitanya-prabhuṁ vande
Śrī Caitanya the Lord I worship
bālo ’pi yad-anugrahāt
a child even by whose mercy
taren nānā-mata-grāha-
may cross of various doctrines crocodiles
vyāptaṁ siddhānta-sāgaram
filled with of conclusions the ocean

1I worship Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, by whose mercy even an ignorant child can cross the ocean of philosophical conclusions, which teems with the crocodiles of various doctrines.1

কৃষ্ণোৎকীর্ত্তনগাননর্ত্তনকলাপাথোজনি-ভ্রাজিতা
সদ্ভক্তাবলিহংসচক্রমধুপশ্রেণীবিহারাস্পদম্ ৷
কর্ণানন্দিকলধ্বনির্বহতু মে জিহ্বামরুপ্রাঙ্গণে
শ্রীচৈতন্যদয়ানিধে তব লসল্লীলাসুধাস্বর্ধুনী ॥ ২ ॥

kṛṣṇotkīrtana-gāna-nartana-kalā-pāthojani-bhrājitā
of Kṛṣṇa loud glorification singing dancing arts lotuses adorned
sad-bhaktāvali-haṁsa-cakra-madhupa-śreṇī-vihārāspadam
of true devotees rows swans cakravāka birds bees swarms of pleasure abode
karṇānandi-kala-dhvanir vahatu me jihvā-maru-prāṅgaṇe
delighting the ears sweet sound may it flow my of the tongue desert over the expanse
śrī-caitanya dayā-nidhe tava lasal-līlā-sudhā-svardhunī
O Śrī Caitanya of mercy ocean Your shining pastimes nectar celestial Gaṅgā

2O Śrī Caitanya, ocean of mercy! May the celestial Gaṅgā of the nectar of Your shining pastimes flow over the desert of my tongue. She is adorned with the lotuses of the loud glorification of Kṛṣṇa, of singing and of dancing; she is the place of delight for the rows of true devotees, who are like swans, cakravāka birds and bees; and her sweet murmur gladdens the ear.2

জয় জয় শ্রীচৈতন্য জয় নিত্যানন্দ ৷
জয়াদ্বৈতচন্দ্র জয় গৌরভক্তবৃন্দ ॥ ৩ ॥

jaya jaya śrī-caitanya jaya nityānanda
glory glory to Śrī Caitanya glory to Nityānanda
jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
glory to Advaitacandra glory of Gaura the devotees to the multitude

3Glory, glory to Śrī Caitanya! Glory to Nityānanda! Glory to Advaitacandra! Glory to all the devotees of Gaura!

তৃতীয় শ্লোকের অর্থ করি বিবরণ ৷
বস্তু-নির্দ্দেশরূপ মঙ্গলাচরণ ॥ ৪ ॥

tṛtīya ślokera artha kari vivaraṇa
of the third verse the meaning I make explanation
vastu-nirdeśa-rūpa maṅgalācaraṇa
the Object indicating in the form of auspicious invocation

4Now I shall explain in detail the meaning of the third verse. It is an auspicious invocation that points to the Supreme Truth (vastu-nirdeśa).3

যদদ্বৈতং ব্রহ্মোপনিষদি তদপ্যস্য তনুভা
য আত্মান্তর্যামী পুরুষ ইতি সোঽস্যাংশবিভবঃ ৷
ষড়ৈশ্বর্য্যৈঃ পূর্ণো য ইহ ভগবান্ স স্বয়ময়ং
ন চৈতন্যাৎ কৃষ্ণাজ্জগতি পরতত্ত্বং পরমিহ ॥ ৫ ॥

yad advaitaṁ brahmopaniṣadi tad apy asya tanu-bhā
which non-dual Brahman in the Upaniṣads that also His bodily effulgence
ya ātmāntar-yāmī puruṣa iti so ’syāṁśa-vibhavaḥ
who the Supersoul the Indweller the Puruṣa thus He His portion manifestation
ṣaḍ-aiśvaryaiḥ pūrṇo ya iha bhagavān sa svayam ayaṁ
with six opulences full who here Bhagavān He Himself this one
na caitanyāt kṛṣṇāj jagati para-tattvaṁ param iha
not than Caitanya Kṛṣṇa in the world supreme truth higher here

5“There is no Truth in the world higher than Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. That which the Upaniṣads call the non-dual Brahman is the effulgence of His body; the Puruṣa, the Supersoul who dwells within every heart, is His partial manifestation; and Bhagavān, full in all six opulences, is He Himself.”4

ব্রহ্ম, আত্মা, ভগবান্ — অনুবাদ তিন ৷
অঙ্গপ্রভা, অংশ, স্বরূপ — তিন বিধেয় চিহ্ন ॥ ৬ ॥

brahma, ātmā, bhagavān — anuvāda tina
Brahman, Paramātmā, Bhagavān — subjects three
aṅga-prabhā, aṁśa, svarūpa — tina vidheya cihna
of the body effulgence, portion, own form — three predicates marks

6Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān are the three anuvādas (that which is spoken of); the effulgence of the body, the partial manifestation and His own form are the three vidheyas (that which is stated about them).5

অনুবাদ আগে, পাছে বিধেয় স্থাপন ৷
সেই অর্থ কহি, শুন শাস্ত্রবিবরণ ॥ ৭ ॥

anuvāda āge, pāche vidheya sthāpana
the subject first, afterwards the predicate placing
sei artha kahi, śuna śāstra-vivaraṇa
that meaning I tell, hear of scripture the explanation

7First the anuvāda is stated, and afterwards the vidheya is set down. In this way I shall tell the meaning of the verse; hear now the explanation according to scripture.

স্বয়ং ভগবান্ কৃষ্ণ, বিষ্ণু-পরতত্ত্ব ৷
পূর্ণজ্ঞান পূর্ণানন্দ পরম মহত্ত্ব ॥ ৮ ॥

svayaṁ bhagavān kṛṣṇa, viṣṇu-paratattva
Himself Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, of Viṣṇu the supreme truth
pūrṇa-jñāna pūrṇānanda parama mahattva
full knowledge full bliss supreme greatness

8Kṛṣṇa is Bhagavān Himself, the supreme truth among all forms of Viṣṇu (viṣṇu-tattva). He is fullness of knowledge, fullness of bliss and the highest greatness.6

‘নন্দসুত’ বলি’ যাঁরে ভাগবতে গাই ৷
সেই কৃষ্ণ অবতীর্ণ চৈতন্য-গোসাঞি ॥ ৯ ॥

‘nanda-suta’ bali’ yām̐re bhāgavate gāi
‘Nanda’s son’ calling whom in the Bhāgavata they sing
sei kṛṣṇa avatīrṇa caitanya-gosāñi
that Kṛṣṇa has descended (as) Caitanya the Lord

9He whom the Bhāgavatam glorifies as the son of Nanda — that same Kṛṣṇa has descended as Śrī Caitanya Gosāñi.

প্রকাশবিশেষে তেঁহ ধরে তিন নাম ৷
ব্রহ্ম, পরমাত্মা আর স্বয়ং ভগবান্ ॥ ১০ ॥

prakāśa-viśeṣe tem̐ha dhare tina nāma
in particular manifestations He bears three names
brahma, paramātmā āra svayaṁ bhagavān
Brahman, Paramātmā and Himself Bhagavān

10In His particular manifestations He bears three names: Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān Himself.

বদন্তি তত্তত্ত্ববিদস্তত্ত্বং যজ্জ্ঞানমদ্বয়ম্ ৷
ব্রহ্মেতি পরমাত্মেতি ভগবানিতি শব্দ্যতে ॥ ১১ ॥

vadanti tat tattva-vidas
they call that of truth the knowers
tattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam
the Truth which knowledge non-dual
brahmeti paramātmeti
Brahman thus Paramātmā thus
bhagavān iti śabdyate
Bhagavān thus is named

11“The knowers of the Truth call the non-dual knowledge the Truth; it is named Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 1.2.11)7

তাঁহার অঙ্গের শুদ্ধ কিরণ-মণ্ডল ৷
উপনিষদ্ কহে তাঁরে ব্রহ্ম সুনির্ম্মল ॥ ১২ ॥

tām̐hāra aṅgera śuddha kiraṇa-maṇḍala
His of the body pure of rays the orb
upaniṣad kahe tām̐re brahma sunirmala
the Upaniṣads call that Brahman most pure

12That which the Upaniṣads call the spotless Brahman is the pure radiance of the rays of His body.

চর্ম্মচক্ষে দেখে যৈছে সূর্য্য নির্ব্বিশেষ ৷
জ্ঞানমার্গে লইতে নারে তাঁহার বিশেষ ॥ ১৩ ॥

carma-cakṣe dekhe yaiche sūrya nirviśeṣa
with fleshly eyes one sees as the sun without features
jñāna-mārge laite nāre tām̐hāra viśeṣa
on the path of knowledge to perceive cannot His particular features

13As the sun appears to fleshly eyes as mere brilliance without features, so on the path of knowledge one cannot perceive His particular features.

যস্য প্রভা প্রভবতো জগদণ্ডকোটি-
কোটিষ্বশেষবসুধাদিবিভূতিভিন্নম্ ৷
তদ্ব্রহ্মনিষ্কলমনন্তমশেষভূতং
গোবিন্দমাদিপুরুষং তমহং ভজামি ॥ ১৪ ॥

yasya prabhā prabhavato jagad-aṇḍa-koṭi-
whose effulgence of the all-mighty of universes of millions
koṭiṣv aśeṣa-vasudhādi-vibhūti-bhinnam
in millions unlimited earths and the like opulences distinct from
tad brahma niṣkalam anantam aśeṣa-bhūtaṁ
that Brahman undivided infinite all-complete
govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
Govinda the original Person Him I worship

14“I worship Govinda, the original Person. Brahman — undivided, infinite and complete, distinct from all the opulences of countless universes, their earths and all else — is the effulgence of Him, the Almighty.” (Brahma-saṁhitā, 5.40)8

কোটী কোটী ব্রহ্মাণ্ডে যে ব্রহ্মের বিভূতি ৷
সেই ব্রহ্ম গোবিন্দের হয় অঙ্গকান্তি ॥ ১৫ ॥

koṭī koṭī brahmāṇḍe ye brahmera vibhūti
millions upon millions in the universes which of Brahman the glory
sei brahma govindera haya aṅga-kānti
that Brahman of Govinda is of the body the radiance

15That Brahman whose glory is spread through millions upon millions of universes is the radiance of Govinda’s body.

সেই গোবিন্দ ভজি আমি, তেঁহো মোর পতি ৷
তাঁহার প্রসাদে মোর হয় সৃষ্টিশক্তি ॥ ১৬ ॥

sei govinda bhaji āmi, tem̐ho mora pati
that Govinda I worship I, He my Lord
tām̐hāra prasāde mora haya sṛṣṭi-śakti
His by the grace to me is of creation the power

16I worship that Govinda; He is my Lord. By His grace I (Brahmā) have the power to create.

মুনয়ো বাতবসনাঃ শ্রমণা ঊর্দ্ধমন্থিনঃ ৷
ব্রহ্মাখ্যং ধাম তে যান্তি শান্তাঃ সন্ন্যাসিনোঽমলাঃ ॥ ১৭ ॥

munayo vāta-vasanāḥ
the sages the wind as clothing
śramaṇā ūrdhva-manthinaḥ
ascetics upward (who keep their seed)
brahmākhyaṁ dhāma te yānti
called Brahman the abode they go to
śāntāḥ sannyāsino ’malāḥ
peaceful renunciants pure

17“Sages clothed by the wind, ascetics who keep their seed drawn upward, peaceful, pure renunciants — they go to the abode called Brahman.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 11.6.47)9

আত্মান্তর্য্যামী যাঁরে যোগশাস্ত্রে কয় ৷
সেহ গোবিন্দের অংশ বিভূতি যে হয় ॥ ১৮ ॥

ātmāntaryāmī yām̐re yoga-śāstre kaya
the Supersoul the Indweller whom in the yoga scriptures they speak of
seha govindera aṁśa vibhūti ye haya
He of Govinda portion manifestation indeed is

18The Supersoul, the Indweller, of whom the scriptures of yoga speak, is a partial manifestation of Govinda.10

অনন্ত স্ফটিকে যৈছে এক সূর্য্য ভাসে ৷
তৈছে জীবে গোবিন্দের অংশ প্রকাশে ॥ ১৯ ॥

ananta sphaṭike yaiche eka sūrya bhāse
in countless crystals as one sun is reflected
taiche jīve govindera aṁśa prakāśe
so in living beings of Govinda the portion is manifest

19As one sun is reflected in countless crystals, so Govinda’s portion, the Supersoul, is manifest in every living being.11

অথবা বহুনৈতেন কিং জ্ঞাতেন তবার্জ্জুন ৷
বিষ্টভ্যাহমিদং কৃৎস্নমেকাংশেন স্থিতো জগৎ ॥ ২০ ॥

atha vā bahunaitena
but or with much this
kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna
what (use) by knowing for you Arjuna
viṣṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛtsnam
pervading I this entire
ekāṁśena sthito jagat
by one portion I stand the universe

20“But what need have you, Arjuna, of all this detailed knowledge? By one portion of Myself I pervade and support this entire universe.” (Bhagavad-gītā, 10.42)12

তমিমমহমজং শরীরভাজাং
হৃদি হৃদি ধিষ্ঠিতমাত্মকল্পিতানাম্ ৷
প্রতিদৃশমিব নৈকধার্কমেকং
সমধিগতোঽস্মি বিধূতভেদমোহঃ ॥ ২১ ॥

tam imam aham ajaṁ śarīra-bhājāṁ
Him this I the unborn of the embodied
hṛdi hṛdi dhiṣṭhitam ātma-kalpitānām
in heart in heart abiding created by Himself
prati-dṛśam iva naikadhārkam ekaṁ
to each eye as if in many ways the sun one
samadhigato ’smi vidhūta-bheda-mohaḥ
have attained I having cast off of difference the illusion

21(Grandsire Bhīṣma said:) “O Śrī Kṛṣṇa! Having cast off the illusion of ‘difference’ between all Your forms, I have attained You, the Unborn, who abide in the heart of each of the embodied beings You have created — like the one sun, which each eye sees in its own way.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 1.9.42)13

সেই ত’ গোবিন্দ সাক্ষাচ্চৈতন্য গোসাঞি ৷
জীব নিস্তারিতে ঐছে দয়ালু আর নাই ॥ ২২ ॥

sei ta’ govinda sākṣāc caitanya gosāñi
that indeed Govinda directly Caitanya the Lord
jīva nistārite aiche dayālu āra nāi
the souls in delivering so merciful another there is not

22That very Govinda is Śrī Caitanya Gosāñi Himself. There is none so merciful in delivering the souls.14

পরব্যোমেতে বৈসে নারায়ণ নাম ৷
ষড়ৈশ্বর্য্যপূর্ণ লক্ষ্মীকান্ত ভগবান্ ॥ ২৩ ॥

para-vyomete vaise nārāyaṇa nāma
in the spiritual sky dwells Nārāyaṇa named
ṣaḍ-aiśvarya-pūrṇa lakṣmī-kānta bhagavān
with six opulences full of Lakṣmī the beloved Bhagavān

23In the spiritual sky dwells the Lord called Nārāyaṇa — Bhagavān, full in the six opulences, the beloved of Lakṣmī.

বেদ, ভাগবত, উপনিষদ্, আগম ৷
‘পূর্ণতত্ত্ব’ যাঁরে কহে, নাহি যাঁর সম ॥ ২৪ ॥

veda, bhāgavata, upaniṣad, āgama
the Vedas, the Bhāgavata, the Upaniṣads, the Āgamas
‘pūrṇa-tattva’ yām̐re kahe, nāhi yām̐ra sama
‘the complete Truth’ whom they call, there is not to whom an equal

24He whom the Vedas, the Bhāgavatam, the Upaniṣads and the Āgamas call “the complete Truth”, and who has no equal —

ভক্তিযোগে ভক্ত পায় যাঁহার দর্শন ৷
সূর্য্য যেন সবিগ্রহ দেখে দেবগণ ॥ ২৫ ॥

bhakti-yoge bhakta pāya yām̐hāra darśana
through bhakti-yoga the devotees attain whose sight
sūrya yena savigraha dekhe deva-gaṇa
the sun as with its form see the gods

25Him the devotees behold through bhakti-yoga, as the gods behold the sun in its own form.15

জ্ঞান-যোগ-মার্গে তাঁরে ভজে যেই সব ৷
ব্রহ্ম-আত্মরূপে তাঁরে করে অনুভব ॥ ২৬ ॥

jñāna-yoga-mārge tām̐re bhaje yei saba
on the path of knowledge and yoga Him worship who all
brahma-ātma-rūpe tām̐re kare anubhava
as Brahman and the Self Him they realise

26Those who worship Him on the paths of knowledge and yoga realise Him as Brahman and as the Supersoul.

উপাসনা-ভেদে জানি ঈশ্বর-মহিমা ৷
অতএব সূর্য্য তাঁর দিয়ে ত’ উপমা ॥ ২৭ ॥

upāsanā-bhede jāni īśvara-mahimā
by the difference of worship I know of the Lord the greatness
ataeva sūrya tām̐ra diye ta’ upamā
therefore the sun for Him is given indeed as a simile

27By the differences in worship we know the greatness of the Lord; that is why He is compared to the sun.

সেই নারায়ণ কৃষ্ণের স্বরূপ অভেদ ৷
একই বিগ্রহ, কিন্তু আকার-বিভেদ ॥ ২৮ ॥

sei nārāyaṇa kṛṣṇera svarūpa abheda
that Nārāyaṇa from Kṛṣṇa’s own form not different
ekai vigraha, kintu ākāra-vibheda
one and the same form, but of shape difference

28That Nārāyaṇa is not different from Kṛṣṇa’s own form: They are one and the same Person, differing only in shape.

ইঁহো ত’ দ্বিভুজ, তিঁহো ধরে চারি হাত ৷
ইঁহো বেণু ধরে, তিঁহো চক্রাদিক সাথ ॥ ২৯ ॥

im̐ho ta’ dvi-bhuja, tim̐ho dhare cāri hāta
this One indeed two-armed, that One holds four hands
im̐ho veṇu dhare, tim̐ho cakrādika sātha
this One the flute holds, that One the disc and the rest with

29This One has two arms, while that One has four; this One holds the flute, that One the disc and the other emblems.16

নারায়ণস্ত্বং ন হি সর্ব্বদেহিনা-
মাত্মাস্যধীশাখিললোকসাক্ষী ৷
নারায়ণোঽঙ্গং নরভূ-জলায়না-
ত্তচ্চাপি সত্যং ন তবৈব মায়া ॥ ৩০ ॥

nārāyaṇas tvaṁ na hi sarva-dehinām
Nārāyaṇa You not indeed of all the embodied
ātmāsy adhīśākhila-loka-sākṣī
the Self You are O Lord of all worlds the witness
nārāyaṇo ’ṅgaṁ nara-bhū-jalāyanāt
Nārāyaṇa (Your) limb from Nara born waters abode
tac cāpi satyaṁ na tavaiva māyā
that also true not Your indeed māyā

30“Are You not Nārāyaṇa? For You are the Self of all embodied beings, O Lord, and the witness of all the worlds. Nārāyaṇa is Your portion — so called because His abode is the waters born of Nara; and that too is true, not Your māyā.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 10.14.14)17

শিশু বৎস হরি’ ব্রহ্মা করি’ অপরাধ ৷
অপরাধ ক্ষমাইতে মাগেন প্রসাদ ॥ ৩১ ॥

śiśu vatsa hari’ brahmā kari’ aparādha
the boys calves having stolen Brahmā having committed offence
aparādha kṣamāite māgena prasāda
the offence to have forgiven begs for mercy

31Having stolen the boys and the calves, Brahmā had committed an offence; to have it forgiven, he begged for mercy:

তোমার নাভিপদ্ম হৈতে আমার জন্মোদয় ৷
তুমি পিতা-মাতা, আমি তোমার তনয় ॥ ৩২ ॥

tomāra nābhi-padma haite āmāra janmodaya
Your of the navel from the lotus my birth
tumi pitā-mātā, āmi tomāra tanaya
You father and mother, I Your son

32“From the lotus of Your navel I was born; You are my father and mother, and I am Your son.

পিতা মাতা বালকের না লয় অপরাধ ৷
অপরাধ ক্ষম, মোরে করহ প্রসাদ ॥ ৩৩ ॥

pitā mātā bālakera nā laya aparādha
father mother of a child do not take the offences
aparādha kṣama, more karaha prasāda
the offence forgive, to me show mercy

33A father and mother do not hold a child’s offences against him. Forgive my offence and be merciful to me.”

কৃষ্ণ কহেন — ব্রহ্মা, তোমার পিতা নারায়ণ ৷
আমি গোপ, তুমি কৈছে আমার নন্দন ॥ ৩৪ ॥

kṛṣṇa kahena — brahmā, tomāra pitā nārāyaṇa
Kṛṣṇa says — Brahmā, your father Nārāyaṇa
āmi gopa, tumi kaiche āmāra nandana
I a cowherd, you how My son

34Kṛṣṇa said: “Brahmā, your father is Nārāyaṇa. I am a cowherd boy — how can you be My son?”

ব্রহ্মা বলেন, তুমি কি না হও নারায়ণ ৷
তুমি নারায়ণ — শুন তাহার কারণ ॥ ৩৫ ॥

brahmā balena, tumi ki nā hao nārāyaṇa
Brahmā says, You whether not are Nārāyaṇa
tumi nārāyaṇa — śuna tāhāra kāraṇa
You Nārāyaṇa — hear of that the reason

35Brahmā said: “Are You not Nārāyaṇa? You are Nārāyaṇa — hear the reason.

প্রাকৃতাপ্রাকৃত-সৃষ্ট্যে যত জীবরূপ ৷
তাহার যে আত্মা তুমি মূল-স্বরূপ ॥ ৩৬ ॥

prākṛtāprākṛta-sṛṣṭye yata jīva-rūpa
in the material and spiritual creation all living forms
tāhāra ye ātmā tumi mūla-svarūpa
their who the Self You the original form

36You are the Self of all living beings, as many as there are in the material and spiritual creation; You are their original source.18

পৃথ্বী যৈছে ঘটকুলের কারণ আশ্রয় ৷
জীবের নিদান তুমি, তুমি সর্ব্বাশ্রয় ॥ ৩৭ ॥

pṛthvī yaiche ghaṭa-kulera kāraṇa āśraya
the earth as of the pots of the multitude the cause the support
jīvera nidāna tumi, tumi sarvāśraya
of the souls the cause You, You of all the shelter

37As the earth is the cause and the support of all earthen pots, so You are the cause of all souls, and You are the shelter of all.

‘নার’ শব্দে কহে সর্ব্বজীবের নিচয় ৷
‘অয়ন’ শব্দেতে কহে তাহার আশ্রয় ॥ ৩৮ ॥

‘nāra’ śabde kahe sarva-jīvera nicaya
‘nāra’ by the word is meant of all souls the aggregate
‘ayana’ śabdete kahe tāhāra āśraya
‘ayana’ by the word is meant their shelter

38The word nāra means the aggregate of all souls, and the word ayana means their shelter.

অতএব তুমি হও মূল নারায়ণ ৷
এই এক হেতু, শুন দ্বিতীয় কারণ ॥ ৩৯ ॥

ataeva tumi hao mūla nārāyaṇa
therefore You are the original Nārāyaṇa
ei eka hetu, śuna dvitīya kāraṇa
this one reason, hear the second reason

39Therefore You are the original Nārāyaṇa. That is one reason; hear now the second.

জীবের ঈশ্বর — পুরুষাদি অবতার ৷
তাঁহা সবা হৈতে তোমার ঐশ্বর্য্য অপার ॥ ৪০ ॥

jīvera īśvara — puruṣādi avatāra
of the souls the lords — the Puruṣas and other avatāras
tām̐hā sabā haite tomāra aiśvarya apāra
Them all than Your majesty unlimited

40The Puruṣas and the other avatāras are the lords of the souls, but Your majesty is unlimited, greater than that of Them all.

অতএব অধীশ্বর তুমি সর্ব্বপিতা ৷
তোমার শক্তিতে তাঁরা জগৎ-রক্ষিতা ॥ ৪১ ॥

ataeva adhīśvara tumi sarva-pitā
therefore the supreme Lord You of all the father
tomāra śaktite tām̐rā jagat-rakṣitā
by Your power They of the world the protectors

41Therefore You are the supreme Lord, the father of all; it is by Your power that They protect the world.

নারের অয়ন যাতে করহ পালন ৷
অতএব হও তুমি মূল নারায়ণ ॥ ৪২ ॥

nārera ayana yāte karaha pālana
of the nāras the shelters since You do protection
ataeva hao tumi mūla nārāyaṇa
therefore are You the original Nārāyaṇa

42Since You protect those who are the shelter of the nāras, You are the original Nārāyaṇa.

তৃতীয় কারণ শুন শ্রীভগবান্ ৷
অনন্ত ব্রহ্মাণ্ড বহু বৈকুণ্ঠাদি ধাম ॥ ৪৩ ॥

tṛtīya kāraṇa śuna śrī-bhagavān
the third reason hear O Śrī Bhagavān
ananta brahmāṇḍa bahu vaikuṇṭhādi dhāma
unlimited universes many Vaikuṇṭhas and other abodes

43Hear the third reason, O Śrī Bhagavān. There are unlimited universes and many abodes — the Vaikuṇṭhas and others.

ইথে যত জীব, তার ত্রৈকালিক কর্ম্ম ৷
তাহা দেখ, সাক্ষী তুমি, জান সব মর্ম্ম ॥ ৪৪ ॥

ithe yata jīva, tāra trai-kālika karma
in them all beings, their of the three times deeds
tāhā dekha, sākṣī tumi, jāna saba marma
that You see, the witness You, You know of all the essence

44All the beings in them, and their deeds in past, present and future — You see it all; You are the witness, You know the heart of everything.

তোমার দর্শনে সর্ব্ব জগতের স্থিতি ৷
তুমি না দেখিলে কার নাহি স্থিতি গতি ॥ ৪৫ ॥

tomāra darśane sarva jagatera sthiti
by Your sight of all worlds the existence
tumi nā dekhile kāra nāhi sthiti gati
You not if You see — of anyone is not rest motion

45By Your glance all the worlds exist; if You did not look on them, nothing could either stand or move.

নারের অয়ন যাতে কর দরশন ৷
তাহাতেও হও তুমি মূল নারায়ণ ॥ ৪৬ ॥

nārera ayana yāte kara daraśana
of the nāras the ways since You do seeing
tāhāteo hao tumi mūla nārāyaṇa
by that also are You the original Nārāyaṇa

46Since You see the ways of all the nāras, by that too You are the original Nārāyaṇa.”

কৃষ্ণ কহেন — ব্রহ্মা, তোমার না বুঝি বচন ৷
জীব-হৃদি, জলে বৈসে সেই নারায়ণ ॥ ৪৭ ॥

kṛṣṇa kahena — brahmā, tomāra nā bujhi vacana
Kṛṣṇa says — Brahmā, your not I understand words
jīva-hṛdi, jale vaise sei nārāyaṇa
in the hearts of beings, in the waters dwells that Nārāyaṇa

47Kṛṣṇa said: “Brahmā, I do not understand your words. Nārāyaṇa is He who dwells in the hearts of living beings and in the waters.”

ব্রহ্মা কহে — জলে জীবে যেই নারায়ণ ৷
সে সব তোমার অংশ, — এ সত্য বচন ॥ ৪৮ ॥

brahmā kahe — jale jīve yei nārāyaṇa
Brahmā says — in the waters in beings who Nārāyaṇa
se saba tomāra aṁśa, — e satya vacana
They all Your portions, — this true word

48Brahmā said: “The Nārāyaṇa who lies in the waters and dwells in the beings — in all these forms He is Your portion. What I say is true.

কারণাব্ধি-গর্ভোদক-ক্ষীরোদকশায়ী ৷
মায়াদ্বারা সৃষ্টি করে, তাতে সব মায়ী ॥ ৪৯ ॥

kāraṇābdhi-garbhodaka-kṣīrodaka-śāyī
of the Causal ocean Garbhodaka Kṣīrodaka who lie
māyā-dvārā sṛṣṭi kare, tāte saba māyī
through māyā creation They do, therefore all masters of māyā

49Kāraṇodakaśāyī, Garbhodakaśāyī and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu create through māyā; therefore all of Them are māyī, masters of māyā.19

সেই তিন জলশায়ী সর্ব্ব-অন্তর্য্যামী ৷
ব্রহ্মাণ্ডবৃন্দের আত্মা যে পুরুষ-নামী ॥ ৫০ ॥

sei tina jala-śāyī sarva-antaryāmī
those three who lie on the waters of all the Indwellers
brahmāṇḍa-vṛndera ātmā ye puruṣa-nāmī
of the universes of the multitude the Self who Puruṣa named

50These three, who lie on the waters, dwell within all as the Supersoul: They who are called Puruṣas are the Self of all the universes.20

হিরণ্যগর্ভের আত্মা গর্ভোদকশায়ী ৷
ব্যষ্টিজীব-অন্তর্য্যামী ক্ষীরোদকশায়ী ॥ ৫১ ॥

hiraṇya-garbhera ātmā garbhodaka-śāyī
of Hiraṇyagarbha the Self Garbhodakaśāyī
vyaṣṭi-jīva-antaryāmī kṣīrodaka-śāyī
of the individual being the Indweller Kṣīrodakaśāyī

51Garbhodakaśāyī is the Self of Hiraṇyagarbha, and Kṣīrodakaśāyī is the Indweller of each individual being.21

এ সভার দর্শনে ত’ আছে মায়াগন্ধ ৷
তুরীয় কৃষ্ণের নাহি মায়ার সম্বন্ধ ॥ ৫২ ॥

e sabhāra darśane ta’ āche māyā-gandha
of Them all in the glance indeed there is of māyā a trace
turīya kṛṣṇera nāhi māyāra sambandha
of the fourth Kṛṣṇa there is not with māyā connection

52They glance upon māyā, and in this there is, as it were, a trace of māyā; but Kṛṣṇa, who abides in the fourth state (turīya), has no connection with māyā at all.22

বিরাট্ হিরণ্যগর্ভশ্চ কারণং চেত্যুপাধয়ঃ ৷
ঈশস্য যৎ ত্রিভির্হীনং তুরীয়ং তৎ প্রচক্ষতে ॥ ৫৩ ॥

virāṭ hiraṇya-garbhaś ca
Virāṭ Hiraṇyagarbha and
kāraṇaṁ cety upādhayaḥ
Kāraṇa thus designations
īśasya yat tribhir hīnaṁ
of the Lord that which of the three devoid
turīyaṁ tat pracakṣate
the fourth that they call

53“Virāṭ, Hiraṇyagarbha and Kāraṇa are designations of the Lord; that which is free from these three is called the fourth (turīya).” (Śrīdhara Svāmī’s commentary on Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 11.15.16)23

যদ্যপি তিনের মায়া লইয়া ব্যবহার ৷
তথাপি তৎস্পর্শ নাহি, সভে মায়া-পার ॥ ৫৪ ॥

yadyapi tinera māyā laiyā vyavahāra
although of the three with māyā having to do dealings
tathāpi tat-sparśa nāhi, sabhe māyā-pāra
yet its touch is not, all beyond māyā

54Although the three have dealings with māyā, she does not touch Them: all of Them are beyond māyā.24

এতদীশনমীশস্য প্রকৃতিস্থোঽপি তদ্গুণৈঃ ৷
ন যুজ্যতে সদাত্মস্থৈর্যথা বুদ্ধিস্তদাশ্রয়া ॥ ৫৫ ॥

etad īśanam īśasya
this the lordship of the Lord
prakṛti-stho ’pi tad-guṇaiḥ
in material nature abiding though by its qualities
na yujyate sadātma-sthair
not is affected ever abiding in Him
yathā buddhis tad-āśrayā
as the intelligence sheltered in Him

55“This is the lordship of the Lord: though He abides within material nature, He is never affected by its qualities — just as the intelligence of those who have taken shelter of Him is not affected.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 1.11.38)

সেই তিন জনের তুমি পরম আশ্রয় ৷
তুমি মূলনারায়ণ — ইথে কি সংশয় ॥ ৫৬ ॥

sei tina janera tumi parama āśraya
those three Persons’ You supreme shelter
tumi mūla nārāyaṇa — ithe ki saṁśaya
You the original Nārāyaṇa — in this what doubt

56You are the supreme shelter of those three; You are the original Nārāyaṇa — what doubt can there be?

সেই তিনের অংশী পরব্যোম-নারায়ণ ৷
তেঁহ তোমার প্রকাশ, তুমি মূল-নারায়ণ ॥ ৫৭ ॥

sei tinera aṁśī paravyoma-nārāyaṇa
of those three the source of the spiritual sky Nārāyaṇa
tem̐ha tomāra prakāśa, tumi mūla-nārāyaṇa
He Your manifestation, You the original Nārāyaṇa

57The source of those three is the Nārāyaṇa of the spiritual sky. He is Your manifestation (prakāśa), and You are the original Nārāyaṇa.”25

অতএব ব্রহ্মবাক্যে পরব্যোম-নারায়ণ ৷
তেঁহ কৃষ্ণের প্রকাশ — এই তত্ত্ব-বিবরণ ॥ ৫৮ ॥

ataeva brahma-vākye paravyoma-nārāyaṇa
therefore of Brahmā in the words of the spiritual sky Nārāyaṇa
tem̐ha kṛṣṇera prakāśa — ei tattva-vivaraṇa
He Kṛṣṇa’s manifestation — this of the truth explanation

58Thus, by Brahmā’s words, the Nārāyaṇa of the spiritual sky is a manifestation of Kṛṣṇa. This is the explanation of the truth.26

এই শ্লোক তত্ত্ব-লক্ষণ ভাগবত-সার ৷
পরিভাষা-রূপে ইহার সর্ব্বত্রাধিকার ॥ ৫৯ ॥

ei śloka tattva-lakṣaṇa bhāgavata-sāra
this verse of the truth characteristic of the Bhāgavata the essence
paribhāṣā-rūpe ihāra sarvatrādhikāra
of a paribhāṣā in the form its everywhere application

59This verse (2.30), which reveals the characteristics of the Truth, is the essence of the Bhāgavatam; as a rule of interpretation (paribhāṣā) it applies everywhere.27

ব্রহ্ম, আত্মা, ভগবান্ — কৃষ্ণের বিহার ৷
এ অর্থ না জানি’ মূর্খ অর্থ করে আর ॥ ৬০ ॥

brahma, ātmā, bhagavān — kṛṣṇera vihāra
Brahman, Paramātmā, Bhagavān — of Kṛṣṇa the manifestations
e artha nā jāni’ mūrkha artha kare āra
this meaning not knowing the foolish meaning make other

60Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān are manifestations of Kṛṣṇa. Not knowing this meaning, fools interpret otherwise.28

অবতারী নারায়ণ, কৃষ্ণ অবতার ৷
তেঁহ চতুর্ভুজ, ইঁহ মনুষ্য-আকার ॥ ৬১ ॥

avatārī nārāyaṇa, kṛṣṇa avatāra
the source of avatāras Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa an avatāra
tem̐ha catur-bhuja, im̐ha manuṣya-ākāra
That One four-armed, this One of human shape

61They say: “Nārāyaṇa is the source of the avatāras, and Kṛṣṇa is His avatāra; for That One has four arms, while this One has a human form.”

এইমতে নানারূপ করে পূর্ব্বপক্ষ ৷
তাহারে নির্জ্জিতে ভাগবত-পদ্য দক্ষ ॥ ৬২ ॥

ei-mate nānā-rūpa kare pūrva-pakṣa
in this way various kinds make objections
tāhāre nirjite bhāgavata-padya dakṣa
them to defeat of the Bhāgavata a verse is expert

62In this way they raise various objections, but a verse of the Bhāgavatam skilfully refutes them.

বদন্তি তত্তত্ত্ববিদস্তত্ত্বং যজ্জ্ঞানমদ্বয়ম্ ৷
ব্রহ্মেতি পরমাত্মেতি ভগবানিতি শব্দ্যতে ॥ ৬৩ ॥

vadanti tat tattva-vidas
they call that of truth the knowers
tattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam
the Truth which knowledge non-dual
brahmeti paramātmeti
Brahman thus Paramātmā thus
bhagavān iti śabdyate
Bhagavān thus is named

63“The knowers of the Truth call the non-dual knowledge the Truth; it is named Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 1.2.11)29

শুন ভাই, এ শ্লোকার্থ করহ বিচার ৷
এক মুখ্যতত্ত্ব, তিন তাহার প্রচার ॥ ৬৪ ॥

śuna bhāi, e ślokārtha karaha vicāra
hear brothers, of this verse’s meaning make consideration
eka mukhya-tattva, tina tāhāra pracāra
one principal Truth, three its manifestations

64Hear, brothers, and consider the meaning of this verse: the principal Truth is one, and It is manifest in three ways.

অদ্বয়জ্ঞান তত্ত্ববস্তু কৃষ্ণের স্বরূপ ৷
ব্রহ্ম, আত্মা, ভগবান্, — তিন তাঁর রূপ ॥ ৬৫ ॥

advaya-jñāna tattva-vastu kṛṣṇera svarūpa
non-dual knowledge the real Truth Kṛṣṇa’s own form
brahma, ātmā, bhagavān, — tina tām̐ra rūpa
Brahman, Paramātmā, Bhagavān, — three His forms

65The non-dual knowledge, the Truth itself, is Kṛṣṇa’s own form; Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān are His three forms.30

এই শ্লোকের অর্থে তুমি হৈলা নির্ব্বচন ৷
আর এক শুন ভাগবতের বচন ॥ ৬৬ ॥

ei ślokera arthe tumi hailā nirvacana
of this verse by the meaning you became speechless
āra eka śuna bhāgavatera vacana
another one hear of the Bhāgavata statement

66The meaning of this verse has left you speechless. Now hear another statement of the Bhāgavatam.

এতে চাংশকলাঃ পুংসঃ কৃষ্ণস্তু ভগবান্ স্বয়ম্ ৷
ইন্দ্রারিব্যাকুলং লোকং মৃড়য়ন্তি যুগে যুগে ॥ ৬৭ ॥

ete cāṁśa-kalāḥ puṁsaḥ
these and portions and parts of the Puruṣa
kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam
Kṛṣṇa but Bhagavān Himself
indrāri-vyākulaṁ lokaṁ
by the enemies of Indra troubled the world
mṛḍayanti yuge yuge
make happy in age after age

67“All these (avatāras) are portions (aṁśa) and parts of portions (kalā) of the Puruṣa, but Kṛṣṇa is Bhagavān Himself. Age after age They bring happiness to the world when it is troubled by the enemies of Indra.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 1.3.28)31

সব অবতারের করি সামান্য-লক্ষণ ৷
তার মধ্যে কৃষ্ণচন্দ্রের করিল গণন ॥ ৬৮ ॥

saba avatārera kari sāmānya-lakṣaṇa
all of the avatāras having made general characteristics
tāra madhye kṛṣṇa-candrera karila gaṇana
their among Kṛṣṇacandra made counting

68Describing the general characteristics of all the avatāras, he counted Kṛṣṇacandra among them.

তবে সূত গোসাঞি মনে পাঞা বড় ভয় ৷
যাঁর যে লক্ষণ তাহা করিল নিশ্চয় ॥ ৬৯ ॥

tabe sūta gosāñi mane pāñā baḍa bhaya
then Sūta Gosāñi in mind feeling great fear
yām̐ra ye lakṣaṇa tāhā karila niścaya
of whom which characteristic that made determination

69Then Sūta Gosāñi, feeling great apprehension in his mind, determined the distinguishing characteristic of each.

অবতার সব — পুরুষের কলা-অংশ ৷
স্বয়ং ভগবান্ কৃষ্ণ সর্ব্ব-অবতংস ॥ ৭০ ॥

avatāra saba — puruṣera kalā-aṁśa
the avatāras all — of the Puruṣa parts portions
svayaṁ bhagavān kṛṣṇa sarva-avataṁsa
Himself Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa of all the crown

70All the avatāras are portions and parts of the Puruṣa, but Kṛṣṇa is Bhagavān Himself, the crown of all.

পূর্ব্বপক্ষ কহে — তোমার ভাল ত’ ব্যাখ্যান ৷
পরব্যোমে-নারায়ণ স্বয়ং ভগবান্ ॥ ৭১ ॥

pūrva-pakṣa kahe — tomāra bhāla ta’ vyākhyāna
the opponent says — your good indeed explanation
paravyome-nārāyaṇa svayaṁ bhagavān
of the spiritual sky Nārāyaṇa Himself Bhagavān

71An opponent says: “Your explanation is fine, but the Nārāyaṇa of the spiritual sky is Bhagavān Himself.

তেঁহ আসি’ কৃষ্ণরূপে করেন অবতার ৷
এই অর্থ শ্লোকে দেখি — কি আর বিচার ॥ ৭২ ॥

tem̐ha āsi’ kṛṣṇa-rūpe karena avatāra
He coming in the form of Kṛṣṇa makes descent
ei artha śloke dekhi — ki āra vicāra
this meaning in the verse I see — what further consideration

72It is He who comes and descends in the form of Kṛṣṇa. This is the meaning I see in the verse — what more is there to consider?”

তারে কহে — কেনে কর কুতর্কানুমান ৷
শাস্ত্রবিরুদ্ধার্থ কভু না হয় প্রমাণ ॥ ৭৩ ॥

tāre kahe — kene kara kutarkānumāna
to him I say — why do you of false logic inferences
śāstra-viruddhārtha kabhu nā haya pramāṇa
to scripture contrary meaning ever not is evidence

73To him I say: “Why do you draw inferences by false logic? A meaning contrary to scripture can never be evidence.

অনুবাদমনুক্ত্বা তু ন বিধেয়মুদীরয়েৎ ৷
ন হ্যলব্ধাস্পদং কিঞ্চিৎ কুত্রচিৎ প্রতিতিষ্ঠতি ॥ ৭৪ ॥

anuvādam anuktvā tu
the subject not having stated but
na vidheyam udīrayet
not the predicate one should utter
na hy alabdhāspadaṁ kiñcit
not indeed without a footing anything
kutracit pratitiṣṭhati
anywhere stands

74‘One should not state the predicate without first stating the subject; for nothing that has not found its footing can stand anywhere.’ (Ekādaśī-tattva, 13)32

অনুবাদ না কহিয়া না কহি বিধেয় ৷
আগে অনুবাদ কহি, পশ্চাদ্বিধেয় ॥ ৭৫ ॥

anuvāda nā kahiyā nā kahi vidheya
the subject not having stated not one states the predicate
āge anuvāda kahi, paścād vidheya
first the subject one states, afterwards the predicate

75Without stating the subject one does not state the predicate: first the subject is stated, and afterwards the predicate.

‘বিধেয়’ কহিয়ে তারে, যে বস্তু অজ্ঞাত ৷
‘অনুবাদ’ কহি তারে, যেই হয় জ্ঞাত ॥ ৭৬ ॥

‘vidheya’ kahiye tāre, ye vastu ajñāta
‘the predicate’ one calls that, which thing unknown
‘anuvāda’ kahi tāre, yei haya jñāta
‘the subject’ one calls that, which is known

76That which is unknown is called the predicate (vidheya); that which is known is called the subject (anuvāda).

যৈছে কহি, — এই বিপ্র পরম পণ্ডিত ৷
বিপ্র — অনুবাদ, ইহার বিধেয় — পাণ্ডিত্য ॥ ৭৭ ॥

yaiche kahi, — ei vipra parama paṇḍita
as we say, — this brāhmaṇa a great scholar
vipra — anuvāda, ihāra vidheya — pāṇḍitya
brāhmaṇa — the subject, its predicate — scholarship

77For example, we say: “This brāhmaṇa is a great scholar.” Here “brāhmaṇa” is the subject, and its predicate is “scholarship”.

বিপ্র বলি’ জানি, তার পাণ্ডিত্য অজ্ঞাত ৷
অতএব বিপ্র আগে, পাণ্ডিত্য পশ্চাৎ ॥ ৭৮ ॥

vipra bali’ jāni, tāra pāṇḍitya ajñāta
a brāhmaṇa that he is we know, his scholarship unknown
ataeva vipra āge, pāṇḍitya paścāt
therefore brāhmaṇa first, scholarship afterwards

78That he is a brāhmaṇa is known, but his scholarship is not; therefore “brāhmaṇa” comes first, and “scholarship” afterwards.

তৈছে ইঁহ অবতার, সব তাঁর জ্ঞাত ৷
কার অবতার — এই বস্তু অবিজ্ঞাত ॥ ৭৯ ॥

taiche im̐ha avatāra, saba tām̐ra jñāta
so here the avatāras, all They known
kāra avatāra — ei vastu avijñāta
of whom avatāras — this thing unknown

79In the same way, here the avatāras are all known, but whose avatāras They are — that is unknown.

‘এতে’ শব্দে অবতারের আগে অনুবাদ ৷
‘পুরুষের অংশ’ পাছে বিধেয় সংবাদ ॥ ৮০ ॥

‘ete’ śabde avatārera āge anuvāda
‘these’ by the word of the avatāras first the subject
‘puruṣera aṁśa’ pāche vidheya saṁvāda
‘of the Puruṣa portions’ afterwards of the predicate the statement

80First, by the word “these”, the avatāras are stated as the subject; afterwards the predicate is given: “portions of the Puruṣa”.33

তৈছে কৃষ্ণ অবতার-ভিতরে হৈল জ্ঞাত ৷
তাঁহার বিশেষ-জ্ঞান সেই অবিজ্ঞাত ॥ ৮১ ॥

taiche kṛṣṇa avatāra-bhitare haila jñāta
so Kṛṣṇa among the avatāras became known
tām̐hāra viśeṣa-jñāna sei avijñāta
of Him particular knowledge that unknown

81So too Kṛṣṇa became known among the avatāras, but the particular knowledge of Him remained unknown.

অতএব ‘কৃষ্ণ’ শব্দ আগে অনুবাদ ৷
‘স্বয়ং ভগবত্তা’ পিছে বিধেয় সংবাদ ॥ ৮২ ॥

ataeva ‘kṛṣṇa’ śabda āge anuvāda
therefore ‘Kṛṣṇa’ the word first the subject
‘svayaṁ bhagavattā’ piche vidheya saṁvāda
‘Bhagavān Himself’ afterwards of the predicate the statement

82Therefore the word “Kṛṣṇa” comes first, as the subject, and afterwards the predicate is stated: that He is “Bhagavān Himself”.

কৃষ্ণের স্বয়ং-ভগবত্তা — ইহা হৈল সাধ্য ৷
স্বয়ং-ভগবানের কৃষ্ণত্ব হৈল বাধ্য ॥ ৮৩ ॥

kṛṣṇera svayaṁ-bhagavattā — ihā haila sādhya
of Kṛṣṇa being Bhagavān Himself — this became established
svayaṁ-bhagavānera kṛṣṇatva haila bādhya
of Bhagavān Himself being Kṛṣṇa became necessary

83Thus it is established that Kṛṣṇa is Bhagavān Himself; and it follows of necessity that Bhagavān Himself is Kṛṣṇa.

কৃষ্ণ যদি অংশ হৈত, অংশী নারায়ণ ৷
তবে বিপরীত হৈত সূতের বচন ॥ ৮৪ ॥

kṛṣṇa yadi aṁśa haita, aṁśī nārāyaṇa
Kṛṣṇa if a portion were, the source Nārāyaṇa
tabe viparīta haita sūtera vacana
then reversed would be of Sūta the statement

84If Kṛṣṇa were the portion and Nārāyaṇa the source, Sūta’s statement would have been the reverse.

নারায়ণ অংশী যেই স্বয়ং-ভগবান্ ৷
তেঁহ শ্রীকৃষ্ণ — ঐছে করি তা ব্যাখ্যান ॥ ৮৫ ॥

nārāyaṇa aṁśī yei svayaṁ-bhagavān
Nārāyaṇa the source who Bhagavān Himself
tem̐ha śrī-kṛṣṇa — aiche kari tā vyākhyāna
He Śrī Kṛṣṇa — so would make that explanation

85He would have said: “Nārāyaṇa, the source, is Bhagavān Himself, and He is Śrī Kṛṣṇa.”

ভ্রম, প্রমাদ, বিপ্রলিপ্সা, করণাপাটব ৷
আর্ষ-বিজ্ঞবাক্যে নাহি দোষ এই সব ॥ ৮৬ ॥

bhrama, pramāda, vipralipsā, karaṇāpāṭava
error, inattention, deceit, imperfection of the senses
ārṣa-vijña-vākye nāhi doṣa ei saba
of the seers wise in the words there are not faults these all

86In the words of the wise seers there are none of these faults: error, inattention, the wish to deceive, and imperfection of the senses.34

বিরুদ্ধার্থ কহ তুমি, কহিতে কর রোষ ৷
তোমার অর্থে অবিমৃষ্টবিধেয়াংশ-দোষ ॥ ৮৭ ॥

viruddhārtha kaha tumi, kahite kara roṣa
contrary meaning speak you, on being told you show anger
tomāra arthe avimṛṣṭa-vidheyāṁśa-doṣa
in your interpretation of the unconsidered predicate the fault

87You speak against the scriptures and grow angry when this is pointed out. The fault in your interpretation is that the predicate is wrongly placed (avimṛṣṭa-vidheyāṁśa).35

যাঁর ভগবত্তা হৈতে অন্যের ভগবত্তা ৷
‘স্বয়ং ভগবান্’ শব্দের তাহাতেই সত্তা ॥ ৮৮ ॥

yām̐ra bhagavattā haite anyera bhagavattā
whose Godhood from of others Godhood
‘svayaṁ bhagavān’ śabdera tāhātei sattā
‘Bhagavān Himself’ of the word in Him alone the meaning

88He from whose Godhood the Godhood of all others proceeds — in Him alone the words “Bhagavān Himself” have their meaning.

দীপ হৈতে যৈছে বহু দীপের জ্বলন ৷
মূল এক দীপ তাহা করিয়ে গণন ॥ ৮৯ ॥

dīpa haite yaiche bahu dīpera jvalana
a lamp from as of many lamps kindling
mūla eka dīpa tāhā kariye gaṇana
original one lamp that I count

89As many lamps are kindled from one lamp, and that one I count as the original,36

তৈছে সব অবতারের কৃষ্ণ সে কারণ ৷
আর এক শ্লোক শুন, কুব্যাখ্যা-খণ্ডন ॥ ৯০ ॥

taiche saba avatārera kṛṣṇa se kāraṇa
so of all avatāras Kṛṣṇa indeed the cause
āra eka śloka śuna, kuvyākhyā-khaṇḍana
another one verse hear, of wrong interpretations refutation

90so Kṛṣṇa is the cause of all the avatāras. Hear another verse, which refutes wrong interpretations.

অত্র সর্গো বিসর্গশ্চ স্থানং পোষণমূতয়ঃ ৷
মন্বন্তরেশানুকথা নিরোধো মুক্তিরাশ্রয়ঃ ॥ ৯১ ॥

দশমস্য বিশুদ্ধ্যর্থং নবানামিহ লক্ষণম্ ৷
বর্ণয়ন্তি মহাত্মানঃ শ্রুতেনার্থেন চাঞ্জসা ॥ ৯২ ॥

atra sargo visargaś ca
here primary creation secondary creation and
sthānaṁ poṣaṇam ūtayaḥ
maintenance favour impulses
manvantareśānukathā
the reigns of Manu narrations of the Lord
nirodho muktir āśrayaḥ
winding up liberation the shelter
daśamasya viśuddhy-arthaṁ
of the tenth for the clear understanding
navānām iha lakṣaṇam
of the nine here the characteristics
varṇayanti mahātmānaḥ
describe the great souls
śrutenārthena cāñjasā
by what is heard by meaning and directly

91–92“In this Bhāgavatam there are ten subjects: primary creation (sarga), secondary creation (visarga), maintenance (sthāna), the Lord’s favour to His devotees (poṣaṇa), the impulses to action (ūti), the reigns of Manu (manvantara), the narrations of the Lord (īśānukathā), the winding up of the world (nirodha), liberation (mukti) and the shelter (āśraya). To reveal clearly the tenth, the great souls describe here the characteristics of the other nine — sometimes in prayers and narratives, sometimes by direct explanation.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 2.10.1–2)37

আশ্রয় জানিতে কহি এ নব পদার্থ ৷
এ নবের উৎপত্তি-হেতু সেই আশ্রয়ার্থ ॥ ৯৩ ॥

āśraya jānite kahi e nava padārtha
the shelter to know I tell these nine categories
e navera utpatti-hetu sei āśrayārtha
of these nine of the origin the cause that the meaning of shelter

93To make the shelter known I have named these nine categories; the cause from which these nine arise — that is what “the shelter” means.

কৃষ্ণ এক সর্ব্বাশ্রয়, কৃষ্ণ সর্ব্বধাম ৷
কৃষ্ণের শরীরে সর্ব্ব-বিশ্বের বিশ্রাম ॥ ৯৪ ॥

kṛṣṇa eka sarvāśraya, kṛṣṇa sarva-dhāma
Kṛṣṇa alone the shelter of all, Kṛṣṇa of all the abode
kṛṣṇera śarīre sarva-viśvera viśrāma
Kṛṣṇa’s in the body of all universes the rest

94Kṛṣṇa alone is the shelter of all; Kṛṣṇa is the abode of all. In Kṛṣṇa’s body all the universes rest.

দশমে দশমং লক্ষ্যমাশ্রিতাশ্রয়বিগ্রহম্ ৷
শ্রীকৃষ্ণাখ্যং পরং ধাম জগদ্ধাম নমামি তৎ ॥ ৯৫ ॥

daśame daśamaṁ lakṣyam
in the Tenth (Canto) the tenth the subject
āśritāśraya-vigraham
of the sheltered the shelter the embodiment
śrī-kṛṣṇākhyaṁ paraṁ dhāma
Śrī Kṛṣṇa named the supreme abode
jagad-dhāma namāmi tat
of the world the abode I bow to That

95“In the Tenth Canto the tenth subject is revealed: the embodiment of the shelter of all who take shelter, the supreme abode named Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the abode of the world. To That I bow down.” (Śrīdhara Svāmī, Bhāvārtha-dīpikā on Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 10.1.1)

কৃষ্ণের স্বরূপ, আর শক্তিত্রয়-জ্ঞান ৷
যাঁর হয়, তাঁর নাহি কৃষ্ণেতে অজ্ঞান ॥ ৯৬ ॥

kṛṣṇera svarūpa, āra śakti-traya-jñāna
of Kṛṣṇa own form, and of the three potencies knowledge
yām̐ra haya, tām̐ra nāhi kṛṣṇete ajñāna
who has, he has not about Kṛṣṇa ignorance

96One who knows Kṛṣṇa’s own form and His three potencies is no longer ignorant of Kṛṣṇa.

কৃষ্ণের স্বরূপের হয় ষড়্বিধ বিলাস ৷
প্রাভব-বৈভব-রূপে দ্বিবিধ প্রকাশ ॥ ৯৭ ॥

kṛṣṇera svarūpera haya ṣaḍ-vidha vilāsa
of Kṛṣṇa of the own form are sixfold pastime forms
prābhava-vaibhava-rūpe dvi-vidha prakāśa
prābhava vaibhava in the forms twofold manifestation

97Kṛṣṇa’s own form has six kinds of pastime forms (vilāsa): His manifestations are of two kinds, prābhava and vaibhava;38

অংশ-শক্ত্যাবেশরূপে দ্বিবিধাবতার ৷
বাল্য-পৌগণ্ড-ধর্ম্ম দুই ত’ প্রকার ॥ ৯৮ ॥

aṁśa-śaktyāveśa-rūpe dvi-vidhāvatāra
portion empowered in the forms twofold avatāras
bālya-paugaṇḍa-dharma dui ta’ prakāra
of childhood of boyhood nature two indeed kinds

98His avatāras are of two kinds, partial (aṁśa) and empowered (śaktyāveśa); and His pastimes are of two kinds, those of childhood (bālya) and of boyhood (paugaṇḍa).39

কিশোরস্বরূপ কৃষ্ণ স্বয়ং অবতারী ৷
ক্রীড়া করে এই ছয়-রূপে বিশ্ব ভরি’ ॥ ৯৯ ॥

kiśora-svarūpa kṛṣṇa svayaṁ avatārī
youthful in His own form Kṛṣṇa Himself the source of avatāras
krīḍā kare ei chaya-rūpe viśva bhari’
pastimes performs in these six forms the universe filling

99Kṛṣṇa in His own form is youthful (kiśora): He Himself is the source of the avatāras. In these six forms He sports, filling the universe.

এই ছয়-রূপে হয় অনন্ত বিভেদ ৷
অনন্তরূপে একরূপ, নাহি কিছু ভেদ ॥ ১০০ ॥

ei chaya-rūpe haya ananta vibheda
in these six forms there are unlimited varieties
ananta-rūpe eka-rūpa, nāhi kichu bheda
in unlimited forms one form, there is not any difference

100Within these six forms there are unlimited varieties; yet in all those unlimited forms there is one form, and no difference at all.

চিচ্ছক্তি, স্বরূপশক্তি, অন্তরঙ্গা নাম ৷
তাহার বৈভব অনন্ত বৈকুণ্ঠাদি ধাম ॥ ১০১ ॥

cic-chakti, svarūpa-śakti, antaraṅgā nāma
the spiritual potency, the personal potency, internal by name
tāhāra vaibhava ananta vaikuṇṭhādi dhāma
its opulence unlimited Vaikuṇṭhas and other abodes

101The spiritual potency (cit-śakti) is also called the personal potency (svarūpa-śakti) and the internal potency (antaraṅgā); her opulence is the unlimited abodes, such as the Vaikuṇṭhas.40

মায়াশক্তি, বহিরঙ্গা, জগৎকারণ ৷
তাহার বৈভব অনন্ত ব্রহ্মাণ্ডের গণ ॥ ১০২ ॥

māyā-śakti, bahiraṅgā, jagat-kāraṇa
the potency māyā, external, of the world the cause
tāhāra vaibhava ananta brahmāṇḍera gaṇa
its opulence unlimited of universes the multitudes

102The potency māyā, the external potency, is the cause of the world: her opulence is the unlimited multitude of universes.

জীবশক্তি তটস্থাখ্য, নাহি যার অন্ত ৷
মুখ্য তিন শক্তি, তার বিভেদ অনন্ত ॥ ১০৩ ॥

jīva-śakti taṭasthākhya, nāhi yāra anta
the potency of souls marginal called, there is not of which an end
mukhya tina śakti, tāra vibheda ananta
principal three potencies, their varieties unlimited

103The potency of the souls, called marginal (taṭasthā), has no end. These are the three principal potencies, and their varieties are unlimited.

এই ত’ স্বরূপগণ, আর তিন শক্তি ৷
সবার আশ্রয় কৃষ্ণ, কৃষ্ণে সবার স্থিতি ॥ ১০৪ ॥

ei ta’ svarūpa-gaṇa, āra tina śakti
these indeed the personal forms, and three potencies
sabāra āśraya kṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇe sabāra sthiti
of all the shelter Kṛṣṇa, in Kṛṣṇa of all the abiding

104Such are His personal forms and His three potencies. Kṛṣṇa is the shelter of them all; in Kṛṣṇa they all abide.

যদ্যপি ব্রহ্মাণ্ডগণের পুরুষ আশ্রয় ৷
সেহ পুরুষাদি সবার কৃষ্ণ মূলাশ্রয় ॥ ১০৫ ॥

yadyapi brahmāṇḍa-gaṇera puruṣa āśraya
although of the universes the Puruṣa the shelter
seha puruṣādi sabāra kṛṣṇa mūlāśraya
of those Puruṣas and others of all Kṛṣṇa the original shelter

105Although the Puruṣa is the shelter of the universes, Kṛṣṇa is the original shelter of all — of the Puruṣas and the rest.

স্বয়ং ভগবান্ কৃষ্ণ, কৃষ্ণ সর্ব্বাশ্রয় ৷
পরম ঈশ্বর কৃষ্ণ সর্ব্বশাস্ত্রে কয় ॥ ১০৬ ॥

svayaṁ bhagavān kṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇa sarvāśraya
Himself Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa the shelter of all
parama īśvara kṛṣṇa sarva-śāstre kaya
the supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa in all scriptures is said

106Kṛṣṇa is Bhagavān Himself; Kṛṣṇa is the shelter of all. All the scriptures declare Kṛṣṇa to be the Supreme Lord.

ঈশ্বরঃ পরমঃ কৃষ্ণঃ সচ্চিদানন্দবিগ্রহঃ ৷
অনাদিরাদির্গোবিন্দঃ সর্ব্বকারণকারণম্ ॥ ১০৭ ॥

īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
the Lord Supreme Kṛṣṇa
sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ
of being knowledge bliss whose form
anādir ādir govindaḥ
without beginning the beginning Govinda
sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam
of all causes the cause

107“Kṛṣṇa, Govinda, is the Supreme Lord; His form is eternal being, knowledge and bliss. He has no beginning, yet He is the beginning of all, the cause of all causes.” (Brahma-saṁhitā, 5.1)

এ সব সিদ্ধান্ত তুমি জান ভালমতে ৷
তবু পূর্ব্বপক্ষ কর আমা চালাইতে ॥ ১০৮ ॥

e saba siddhānta tumi jāna bhāla-mate
these all conclusions you know well
tabu pūrva-pakṣa kara āmā cālāite
yet objections you make me to unsettle

108You know all these conclusions well, and yet you raise objections, only to unsettle me.41

সেই কৃষ্ণ অবতারী ব্রজেন্দ্রকুমার ৷
আপনে চৈতন্যরূপে কৈল অবতার ॥ ১০৯ ॥

sei kṛṣṇa avatārī vrajendra-kumāra
that Kṛṣṇa the source of avatāras of the king of Vraja the son
āpane caitanya-rūpe kaila avatāra
Himself in the form of Caitanya made descent

109That Kṛṣṇa, the source of all avatāras, the son of the king of Vraja, has Himself descended in the form of Caitanya.

অতএব চৈতন্য-গোসাঞি পরতত্ত্ব-সীমা ৷
তাঁরে ক্ষীরোদশায়ী কহি, কি তাঁর মহিমা ॥ ১১০ ॥

ataeva caitanya-gosāñi paratattva-sīmā
therefore Caitanya Gosāñi of the Supreme Truth the limit
tām̐re kṣīroda-śāyī kahi, ki tām̐ra mahimā
Him Kṣīrodaśāyī calling, what His glory

110Therefore Caitanya Gosāñi is the furthest limit of the Supreme Truth. To call Him Kṣīrodaśāyī — what glory is that to Him?42

সেই ত’ ভক্তের বাক্য নহে ব্যভিচারী ৷
সকল সম্ভবে তাঁতে, যাতে অবতারী ॥ ১১১ ॥

sei ta’ bhaktera vākya nahe vyabhicārī
that indeed of the devotee the word is not erroneous
sakala sambhave tām̐te, yāte avatārī
all is possible in Him, since the source of avatāras

111Yet such words of a devotee are not wrong: everything is possible in Him, for He is the source of the avatāras.

অবতারীর দেহে সব অবতারের স্থিতি ৷
কেহো কোনমতে কহে, যেমন যার মতি ॥ ১১২ ॥

avatārīra dehe saba avatārera sthiti
of the source of avatāras in the body of all avatāras the presence
keho kona-mate kahe, yemana yāra mati
someone in some way speaks, according as whose understanding

112All the avatāras are present in the body of their source; so each speaks of Him in his own way, according to his understanding.

কৃষ্ণকে কহয়ে কেহ — নরনারায়ণ ৷
কেহো কহে, কৃষ্ণ হয় সাক্ষাৎ বামন ॥ ১১৩ ॥

kṛṣṇake kahaye keha — nara-nārāyaṇa
Kṛṣṇa calls someone — Nara-Nārāyaṇa
keho kahe, kṛṣṇa haya sākṣāt vāmana
someone says, Kṛṣṇa is directly Vāmana

113Some call Kṛṣṇa Nara-Nārāyaṇa; others say that Kṛṣṇa is Vāmana Himself.

কেহো কহে, কৃষ্ণ ক্ষীরোদশায়ী অবতার ৷
অসম্ভব নহে, সত্য বচন সবার ॥ ১১৪ ॥

keho kahe, kṛṣṇa kṣīroda-śāyī avatāra
someone says, Kṛṣṇa of Kṣīrodaśāyī an avatāra
asambhava nahe, satya vacana sabāra
impossible it is not, true the words of all

114Some say that Kṛṣṇa is an avatāra of Kṣīrodaśāyī. Nothing of this is impossible; the words of all of them are true.

কেহো কহে, পরব্যোমে নারায়ণ-হরি ৷
সকল সম্ভবে কৃষ্ণে, যাতে অবতারী ॥ ১১৫ ॥

keho kahe, para-vyome nārāyaṇa-hari
someone says, in the spiritual sky Nārāyaṇa Hari
sakala sambhave kṛṣṇe, yāte avatārī
all is possible in Kṛṣṇa, since the source of avatāras

115Some call Him Nārāyaṇa, Hari of the spiritual sky. Everything is possible in Kṛṣṇa, for He is the source of the avatāras.

সব শ্রোতাগণের করি চরণ বন্দন ৷
এ সব সিদ্ধান্ত শুন, করি’ এক মন ॥ ১১৬ ॥

saba śrotā-gaṇera kari caraṇa vandana
of all the listeners I make to the feet obeisance
e saba siddhānta śuna, kari’ eka mana
these all conclusions hear, making one-pointed the mind

116I bow down at the feet of all my listeners: hear all these conclusions with undivided attention.

সিদ্ধান্ত বলিয়া চিত্তে না কর অলস ৷
ইহা হৈতে কৃষ্ণে লাগে সুদৃঢ় মানস ॥ ১১৭ ॥

siddhānta baliyā citte nā kara alasa
conclusions thinking them in the mind not be idle
ihā haite kṛṣṇe lāge sudṛḍha mānasa
from this to Kṛṣṇa becomes attached firmly the mind

117Do not be indifferent to them, thinking them mere doctrine; from them the mind becomes firmly attached to Kṛṣṇa.

চৈতন্য-মহিমা জানি এ সব সিদ্ধান্তে ৷
চিত্ত দৃঢ় হঞা লাগে মহিমা-জ্ঞান হৈতে ॥ ১১৮ ॥

caitanya-mahimā jāni e saba siddhānte
Caitanya’s greatness I know by these all conclusions
citta dṛḍha hañā lāge mahimā-jñāna haite
the mind firm becoming is attached of greatness knowledge from

118Through all these conclusions I come to know the greatness of Caitanya; and from knowing His greatness the mind becomes firm and attached to Him.43

চৈতন্যপ্রভুর মহিমা কহিবার তরে ৷
কৃষ্ণের মহিমা কহি করিয়া বিস্তারে ॥ ১১৯ ॥

caitanya-prabhura mahimā kahibāra tare
Caitanya the Lord’s greatness to tell for the sake of
kṛṣṇera mahimā kahi kariyā vistāre
Kṛṣṇa’s greatness I tell making in detail

119To tell the greatness of Caitanya Prabhu, I have described the greatness of Kṛṣṇa in detail.

চৈতন্য-গোসাঞির এই তত্ত্ব-নিরূপণ ৷
স্বয়ং ভগবান্ কৃষ্ণ ব্রজেন্দ্রনন্দন ॥ ১২০ ॥

caitanya-gosāñira ei tattva-nirūpaṇa
Caitanya Gosāñi’s this of the truth determination
svayaṁ bhagavān kṛṣṇa vrajendra-nandana
Himself Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa of the king of Vraja the son

120This is the determination of the truth of Caitanya Gosāñi: He is Bhagavān Himself, Kṛṣṇa, the son of the king of Vraja.

শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ৷
চৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥ ১২১ ॥

śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
Śrī Rūpa’s, Raghunātha’s at the feet whose hope
caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
“Caitanya-caritāmṛta” narrates Kṛṣṇadāsa

121Praying at the feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate the Caitanya-caritāmṛta.

✦

Notes

  1. Anubhāṣya: bālaḥ — “an inexperienced child”; the crocodiles are the mutually contending doctrines of Aulūkya, Jina, Buddha, Jaimini, Patañjali, Gautama, Kaṇāda, Kapila, Śaṅkara, Dattātreya and others; by the Lord’s mercy even the inexperienced one sets them aside as straw and comes to know the pure feet of Kṛṣṇa.
  2. Anubhāṣya: the swans, cakravākas and bees are pure devotees in different moods (bhāva), for whom these pastimes are a place of supreme joy; the murmur of the river is the sweet, indistinct sound of the stream of Śrī Hari’s pastimes, sung by His devotees.
  3. Indicating the Object (vastu-nirdeśa) is one of the three kinds of auspicious invocation (Ādi 1.22). In the edition the verse is headed: “explanation of the third of the first fourteen verses — indicating the Object”.
  4. The same verse as Ādi 1.3. Anubhāṣya: Brahman is the radiance of His transcendental body, and the Paramātmā a particular manifestation of His majesty; both are only two aspects of His form, perceived according to the capacity of the seer — not the fullness of the Lord, as Bhagavān is. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: “He whom they call Bhagavān, the shelter and source of Brahman and Paramātmā, is my Lord, Bhagavān Himself.”
  5. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: by the rules of rhetoric one first names the anuvāda, the known, and then the vidheya, the new. That Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān exist is known from the Vedas; that Brahman is the effulgence of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya’s body, Paramātmā His portion and Bhagavān He Himself, is not yet known — and this is what is stated.
  6. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: “The conclusion of the scriptures is this: the supreme truth of viṣṇu-tattva is Bhagavān Himself, Kṛṣṇacandra.”
  7. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the first realisation of that non-dual knowledge is Brahman, the second Paramātmā, the third Bhagavān.
  8. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: “… the Brahman distinct from the unlimited opulences — earths and the rest — in millions upon millions of universes, undivided, infinite and complete, has arisen from the effulgence of that original Person, Govinda.”
  9. Anubhāṣya: with this verse it is shown that attaining Kṛṣṇa’s feet is easy, whereas renunciants who labour hard attain, as the fruit of their practice, only the realm of Brahman; vāta-vasanāḥ — naked; śramaṇāḥ — mendicants who emaciate the body; brahmākhyam — featureless.
  10. Anubhāṣya: the Puruṣa who dwells within is the Paramātmā, “only a manifestation of a portion (aṁśa-vibhūti) of Govinda”; the three Puruṣa-avatāras govern the material world, while Bhagavān Himself, abiding in the fourth, turīya, is attached to none of its affairs.
  11. Anubhāṣya: the one Śrī Govinda, ever manifest in Goloka-Vṛndāvana, appears in the hearts of countless souls as the Paramātmā, the Person whom the soul is to serve.
  12. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: “by one portion, as the Paramātmā, I have entered and abide in the whole world.”
  13. Anubhāṣya: bheda-mohaḥ — the illusion that the Lord’s forms (prakāśa, vilāsa) differ in name, form, qualities and pastimes; ātma-kalpitānām — “created by Himself”. Reference to the Bhāgavatam as in the edition.
  14. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: by the word sākṣāt (“directly, Himself”) the author establishes that Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is Govinda Himself, not His prakāśa or vilāsa.
  15. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the eternal form of the Lord cannot be seen by material senses or by the efforts of knowledge; through bhakti, through love, only the devotees become fit to see it — as the gods, whose divine eyes pierce the net of the sun’s rays, see the sun’s own form.
  16. As in the Gauḍīya Maṭha edition: «চারি হাত» (another spelling: «হাথ»).
  17. Anubhāṣya: the verse gives three meanings of the name Nārāyaṇa, corresponding to the three Puruṣa-avatāras: “the Self of all the embodied” (nāra — the aggregate of souls, ayana — their shelter) is Kṣīrodakaśāyī; “the witness of all the worlds” (ayase — “You know”) is Garbhodakaśāyī; “He whose abode is the waters born of Nara” is Kāraṇodakaśāyī. All of Them are Your portions, and You are the original Nārāyaṇa. “Not māyā” — not transient like what māyā produces: māyā cannot touch Your spiritual body, even in the avatāras.
  18. This is the first reason why Kṛṣṇa is the original Nārāyaṇa: nāra — all souls, ayana — their shelter (2.38). Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the material creation lies within māyā (Gītā 7.4–5).
  19. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: “Because They create through māyā, these three Puruṣas are māyī, that is, lords in relation to māyā.” Māyā does not touch Them (2.54).
  20. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: ye puruṣa-nāmī — “They whose name is Puruṣa”. The Self of the universes in this verse is all three of Them: Kāraṇodakaśāyī of all the universes together, Garbhodakaśāyī of the aggregate of beings in a universe, Kṣīrodakaśāyī of each individual being (2.51).
  21. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: Hiraṇyagarbha is the aggregate of beings (samaṣṭi); its Indweller is Garbhodakaśāyī; the Indweller of each separate being (vyaṣṭi) is Kṣīrodakaśāyī.
  22. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: beyond the three Puruṣas is the turīya, “the fourth”: Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the spiritual sky, the vilāsa of Kṛṣṇacandra, utterly free from any trace of māyā; and the Puruṣas, as it says on 2.54, “only cast Their glance upon māyā, but do not touch it”.
  23. Anubhāṣya: Virāṭ is the gross, Hiraṇyagarbha the subtle, Kāraṇa — ignorance or prakṛti; these are particular manifestations (upādhi) of the Puruṣa-avatāra, the creator of the mahat; the turīya, free from them, is Vaikuṇṭha, beyond the three Puruṣas. Śrīdhara Svāmī cites this verse to explain the word turīya.
  24. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: Hiraṇyagarbha and the other beings, collective and individual, are under māyā; the three Puruṣas, though dealing with her, are beyond her — They are lords of māyā; They glance at her, but do not touch her.
  25. As in the Gauḍīya Maṭha edition: «তেঁহ তোমার প্রকাশ» — “He is Your manifestation”. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the Nārāyaṇa of the spiritual sky is the source of the Puruṣa-avatāras; He is “Your secondary manifestation (gauṇa-prakāśa) in the form of vilāsa”. Anubhāṣya: His vilāsa is the fourfold form — Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha — from whom the three Puruṣas appear.
  26. As in the Gauḍīya Maṭha edition: «তেঁহ কৃষ্ণের প্রকাশ» (another reading: «তেঁহো কৃষ্ণের বিলাস»). In meaning this manifestation is a vilāsa: on 2.57 the Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya calls Nārāyaṇa “a secondary manifestation in the form of vilāsa”.
